name: Tsomoriri Camp and Resort
why_it_matters: Five concrete rooms and fifteen deluxe tents at the entrance to Korzok village, with a single big dining hall that feeds the whole camp at fixed sittings. Half-board is built into the tariff because there are no à la carte options at 4,595m — you eat what the kitchen cooks that night, served hot, served fast.
insider_tip: Dinner is buffet-style and lands by 7:30pm — the kitchen winds down early because staff sleep in heated tents themselves. Skip food expectations and order an extra thermos of hot water for your room; it doubles as a hot-water bottle through the night.

name: Tsomoriri Hotel Lake View
signature_dish: buffet dinner with rotis and mixed vegetable
why_it_matters: TripAdvisor's #1-ranked small hotel in Karzok, with 19 lakefront rooms and an on-site restaurant that does Ladakhi, North Indian, Chinese and continental — unusually broad for the village. The buffets here run by the same kitchen that serves the rooms, so the food is the most consistent in Korzok.
insider_tip: Power runs roughly 7-11pm only; eat dinner early enough that the lights are still on. The morning omelette is the sleeper hit — they have a real cooking gas line, not the kerosene stoves the camps use.
signature_address: Karzok village 194101, Tso Moriri Lake, Leh District, Ladakh

name: Karzok Eco Lounge
why_it_matters: Eco-resort built with local stone and traditional Changpa methods, with an in-house restaurant pitched at travellers who want Ladakhi rather than mainland-Indian food. The kitchen leans into the village's own dishes — skyu, thukpa, tingmo — using produce hauled up from Leh weekly.
insider_tip: Ask for the Ladakhi set meal rather than the menu — the kitchen does that better than the continental breakfasts. Butter tea is real po cha here, not a hotel approximation; warn your stomach if you've never had it.
signature_address: Korzok village, Tso Moriri, Leh District, Ladakh 194101

name: TUTC Tso Moriri Camp
why_it_matters: Mobile luxury camp from The Ultimate Travelling Camp — the same operator behind Chamba Camp Thiksey and Diskit — pitched on request only with a two-night minimum. Each canvas pavilion has en-suite bathrooms with teak wardrobes; dinners run on a chef's set menu around fire-lit common tents, with wines and a sommelier flown in for the season.
insider_tip: Dining is open to in-house guests only and runs purely on a chef's set menu — there is no walk-in, no à la carte. Book the Tsomoriri leg as part of TUTC's Thiksey + Diskit + Pangong combination; standalone two-night requests are often declined in shoulder season.
signature_address: Mobile camp, Korzok plain, Tso Moriri Lake, Leh District, Ladakh 194101
